note: CROSS-LANGUAGE PARITY FIXTURE for payment amount resolution. resolvePaymentAmount exists twice:
in @lukeflow/form-core (TypeScript) and in luke-core-engine PaymentAmountResolver (Java, the one
that actually decides what a card is charged). Every case below runs in BOTH:
Schema per case: entity 'pay' (type payment, attributes {key:'pay', ...payment}) unless payment is
null, plus every entity in sets[use]. If `payIn` names a set entity, 'pay' is appended to that
entity's children; otherwise 'pay' leads root. root = ['pay'?] + the set ids that appear in NO set
entity's children (children entries read as keys: strings as-is, non-negative integers as text),
sorted, minus any id in `omitFromRoot` (which may name 'pay').
With `entitiesAsArray`, entities is an ARRAY: 'pay' first, then the set entities in sorted id order;
every id is then replaced by its array position as text, in root and in children (unless
`arrayKeepIds`, which keeps the original ids — which the renderer cannot resolve).
With `numericRoot`, root entries made only of digits are written as JSON numbers.
`expect` is asserted exactly: ok, and amountMinor/currency/quantity/mode when present, else reason.
